articles.title: Microsoft outage hits millions worldwide; company says fixes not 'working as expected'
articles.description: Microsoft is currently experiencing an outage affecting its email and cloud services due to server failures. Nearly 130,000 users worldwide have reported connectivity issues with Outlook and Teams. The company has identified elevated load as a contributing factor but not due to increased user traffic. Federal agencies in Australia have also reported disruptions in communication due to the outage.

Appeal Extends Property Dispute: Alabama Power appeals; easement case remains unresolved
articles.description: A legal clash continues between Alabama Power and landowner Fenn Church over a transmission line easement. Alabama Power has appealed to the state Supreme Court after a judge refused its request for a temporary restraining order. Church is disputing the compensation for the easement while contesting the company's access to his property, as the work to construct a 74-mile transmission line faces potential delays threatening its May 2027 completion.

articles.title: Bearadise Halloween Attraction: Florida DIY haunt grows to 5,000 sq ft; adds Salem witch-trial history
articles.description: Bearadise in Orange Park has evolved from a simple display into a beloved Halloween destination over the years. Crafted by Matt McCary, this immersive attraction features a graveyard, eerie tombstones, and haunting sound effects. With a nod to history, QR codes reveal insights about the Salem witch trials, ensuring an educational twist. This community-driven experience attracts around 250 trick-or-treaters annually, solidifying its status as a cherished neighborhood tradition.

articles.title: 18th Annual Gala: Toronto event raises over $700,000; gang violence disrupts Haiti students’ schooling
articles.description: Olivia Wilde's collaboration with Artists for Peace and Justice is pivotal in revolutionizing educational access for Haitian children. Following the devastating earthquake in 2010, the organization launched a free school in Port-au-Prince and now assists over 1,400 students each year. Despite ongoing gang violence hindering educational efforts, recent fundraising initiatives have generated substantial support, underscoring the vital need for continued investment in children's education and healthcare in Haiti.

articles.title: Nostalgic Brisbane Home Purchase: Buyer pays A$4.9m for childhood Queenslander; sale bucks weak auction market
articles.description: A remarkable Queenslander residence located in Newmarket, Brisbane, was sold for A$4.9 million following an auction. The buyer, who has local roots, had no intention of bidding initially but ultimately decided to secure the property. This six-bedroom home, featuring expansive views of the city, marks a significant sale in a currently sluggish property market influenced by rising interest rates and borrowing challenges.

articles.title: Can plastic help heal wounds? University of Queensland researchers develop a new biodegradable hydrogel with medical potential
articles.description: Researchers at Australia's University of Queensland have transformed brittle, biodegradable bioplastic PHB into a water-absorbing hydrogel using gamma radiation and polymer grafting. The new material, called P3HB-HEAA, offers improved mechanical properties and could eventually be explored for wound dressings, tissue engineering, drug delivery and surgical applications. Led by PhD candidate Cole Walchle, the research highlights new possibilities for sustainable medical materials. However, further studies are needed to establish its biodegradability and medical suitability.

articles.title: Can students track the secret lives of butterflies and lizards? Georgia Tech is using tiny sensors weighing just 0.03 grams to turn its campus into a living laboratory
articles.description: Georgia Tech is turning its campus into a living laboratory where students will track lizards, birds and butterflies using miniature wireless sensors. One device weighs just 0.03 grams, making it small enough to attach to a lizard. The initiative, led by biology professors Benjamin Freeman and James Stroud, aims to involve more than 800 students annually across disciplines. Researchers also hope to create a dynamic campus biodiversity map within five years, supporting urban wildlife conservation.

articles.title: NSUI stages protest against hazardous air pollution in Delhi, demands immediate action
articles.description: NSUI held a protest in Delhi against air pollution and called for government intervention to protect public health. Led by Vinod Jakhar, students raised concerns about the severe impacts on residents, particularly vulnerable groups. Protesters demanded concrete actions and accountability from authorities to address the worsening situation. Members highlighted access to clean air as a fundamental right that needs urgent attention.

articles.description: Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' has surpassed the Rs 1,000 crore milestone in global earnings.
